direction: Flow matching versus denoising diffusion on 2D toy distributions (eight Gaussians, two moons, checkerboard) with the same small MLP: sample quality as a function of the number of sampling steps (1 to 100), measured with a sliced Wasserstein distance and an MMD against held-out samples. Does the straighter path of flow matching give better few-step samples, and what does a rectified-flow style reflow step add?

decisions.decision: Training budget cut to 3000 it x 512 (from 5000) to fit ~30 min total; shared by all systems. 5 seeds main, 3 seeds ablations. Checkpoints cached so sampler variants share one trained model; the reflow teacher is the seed's FM model.

Driver partitions A and B were accidentally started twice concurrently (4 processes for ~15 min, briefly over the 2-process limit); each (system,task,seed) was logged twice with bit-identical metrics (deterministic seeds), and one duplicate row failed from a file race. Kept the earliest ok row per key, moved the 89 other rows to results/runs_duplicates_removed.jsonl so n=5 seeds, not 10.

H2 was registered as 'ratio closer to 1'; I apply it literally as |r-1| on seed-mean ratios and also disclose the log-ratio reading because the moons case flips sign. Earlier decision text said 89 duplicate rows removed; the correct count is 88.

Audit round: intro gap restated as a controlled 2D replication (Lipman et al. use one architecture for all compared models); exploratory paired tests (K=100 gap, MMD@4, ancestral, Heun at equal NFE) added as a separate table computed by experiments/analyze.py and marked not registered; no new experiment runs.
